I feel like greatest might be stretching things a bit far. I did like the concept behind it, but I think their execution was really poorly done.

First off, if they'd allowed API access to it, so you could have a program promote posts to multiple social network services (like what a few of my friends do so they can tweet and facebook the same message) it would have encouraged people to maintain a google+ account.

Second of all, they really flubbed the Limited Beta approach. While that worked awesomely for gmail, they really dropped the ball for G+. For one, Gmail still worked even if your friends weren't on gmail. you could still email them even if they hadn't gotten in. A social network however, that needs content. If your friends are all still locked out, where are you going to get that content from? Instead they should have given you X invites along with your account, the way gmail did, so that you could instantly convert friends to G+

Third, though I like the improved privacy that G+ offers, I think it actually hurts the appearance of activity on Google+. I'm not sure how you improve that without ditching a feature I really like.

Fourth, they never really treated it like a facebook killer. Instead they were too focused on merging all of their google toys to a plus-environment. I never wanted to integrate with my youtube account, I didn't want my plus to have anything to do with my docs. What I DID want, was a less-evil facebook. Now? my G+ is mostly idle, and I'm back to FB to stalk my friends who are there.

Fifth, they fought their users way way way too hard on the Real Name thing. They could have leveraged that into an advantage. They could have used it as a reason to switch to google+ instead of begrudgingly allowing us to choose the name we want to use.
